description: Colorado-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Colorado's statutory speed in a business district is
questions.explanation: Section 42-4-1101(2)(b) makes 25 miles per hour lawful in any business district, as defined in section 42-1-102(11), except when a special hazard requires a lower speed.

questions.q: Colorado's statutory speed in a residence district is
questions.explanation: Section 42-4-1101(2)(c) makes 30 miles per hour lawful in any residence district, as defined in section 42-1-102(80), except when a special hazard requires a lower speed.

questions.q: On a narrow, winding mountain highway or a blind curve, Colorado's statutory speed is
questions.explanation: Section 42-4-1101(2)(a) makes 20 miles per hour lawful on narrow, winding mountain highways or on blind curves. Open mountain highways are a separate 40 mph rule in subsection (2)(d).

questions.q: Colorado's statutory speed on surfaced four-lane highways that are on the interstate system, or that are freeways or expressways, is
options: 75 mph as the ordinary statutory speed
questions.explanation: Section 42-4-1101(2)(g) makes 65 miles per hour lawful on surfaced four-lane highways on the interstate system or that are freeways or expressways. Other open highways that are not interstate and are not surfaced four-lane freeways or expressways are 55 under subsection (2)(f).

questions.q: CDOT and a local authority may not authorize a Colorado speed limit above
questions.explanation: Section 42-4-1102 says the department shall not authorize a speed in excess of 75 miles per hour, and a local authority shall not authorize a speed in excess of 75 miles per hour. The General Assembly's speed-limit summary states the same ceiling.

questions.q: An adult Colorado driver age 21 or over is suspended for point accumulation of
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue point-suspension page, applying section 42-2-127, lists 12 or more points within any 12 months or 18 or more within any 24 months for an adult 21 or over. Points are counted from the dates of violation.

questions.q: For a Colorado driver 17 or under, the Department of Revenue lists suspension at
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue page for minor drivers 17 and under lists 6 or more points within any 12 months, or 7 or more at any point while under 18. That matches section 42-2-127's thresholds of more than five points in 12 consecutive months and more than six points for violations before age 18.

questions.q: For a Colorado driver ages 18 through 21, suspension points include
options: The same 12-and-18 schedule used for drivers over 21
9 in 12 months, 12 in 24 months, or 14 total
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue lists those three brackets for a minor driver 18 through 21. Section 42-2-127 states the nine-point, twelve-point, and fourteen-point brackets for a minor driver eighteen or older. 9 or more within any 12 months, 12 or more within any 24 months, or 14 or more at any point between ages 18 and 21.

questions.q: A Colorado minor instruction permit for ages 15 to 15 years 6 months requires
options: A road test before the permit is issued
50 hours before the permit is issued
questions.explanation: The Colorado DMV minor-permit page says ages 15 to 15 years 6 months must successfully complete a 30-hour driver education course and pass the written test. Permit holders must drive with a licensed driver over the age of 21.

questions.q: Before a Colorado license at ages 16 to 16 years 6 months, the driver must
options: Hold a 12-month permit, log 50 hours, 10 at night
Hold a permit for 6 months and log 20 hours
Log 40 hours with no night requirement
Skip the drive log if a parent signs a waiver
questions.explanation: The Colorado DMV minor-license page requires a valid permit for at least 12 months and Drive Time Log Sheets showing 50 hours, at least 10 at night, signed by a parent, guardian, or other responsible adult. It also requires behind-the-wheel training and a drive test with an approved driver education school for that age group.

questions.q: During the first year of a Colorado license, a driver under 18 may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless
options: A listed exception applies, such as work
Only a police officer is in the car
questions.explanation: The Colorado DMV minor-license page lists those exceptions to the first-year midnight-to-5 a.m. restriction. An exception on the DMV page applies, including a parent or legal guardian, a school trip when the school does not provide transportation and a signed school statement is carried, work with a signed employer statement, a medical emergency, or the driver is an emancipated minor.

questions.q: Colorado's passenger rule for a newly licensed driver under 18 is
options: For 6 months, only 21+ riders, plus siblings
One passenger under 21 from the first day
Only family members for two years
questions.explanation: The DMV minor-license page says that for the first six months only passengers 21 or older may ride, during the second six months one passenger under 21 may ride, and after one year or at age 18 more than one passenger under 21 is allowed. Siblings may ride at any time, and a medical emergency also allows passengers under 21.

questions.q: In Colorado, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Colorado issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Colorado car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Colorado complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Colorado requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Colorado teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Colorado requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Colorado: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Get Your Colorado Permit and Driver License (Under 21)

questions.q: In Colorado, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Colorado, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Get Your Colorado Permit and Driver License (Under 21)

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Colorado not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Colorado restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Colorado new drivers: off the road Midnight to 5 a.m..

questions.q: In Colorado, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Colorado, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Colorado, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Colorado, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Colorado sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Colorado, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Colorado brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Colorado, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Colorado?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Colorado can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Colorado rural interstate: up to 75 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Colorado's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Colorado: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: The Hands-Free Law — Colorado Department of Transportation

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Colorado?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Colorado, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Colorado left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

provenance.manual: Get Your Colorado Permit and Driver License (Under 21)

questions.q: How is Colorado's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Colorado seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: What is Colorado's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Colorado requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $15,000.

provenance.manual: Welcome to Colorado | Department of Revenue - Motor Vehicle

questions.q: Under Colorado's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Colorado can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
